title: Zariski to etale pullback preserves derived Hom from pseudo-coherent complexes
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Write $\epsilon_X:(X_{\mathrm{et}},\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}})\to(X_{\mathrm{Zar}},\mathcal O_X)$ for the canonical morphism of ringed sites and use its exact module pullback $\epsilon_X^*$ [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Let $K,L\in D(\mathcal O_X)$, with $K$ pseudo-coherent [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex] and $H^i(L)=0$ for every $i<a$ for some integer $a$. The canonical pullback comparison is a natural isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}})$:
$$\epsilon_X^*R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_X}(K,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_{\mathcal O_{X,\mathrm{et}}}(\epsilon_X^*K,\epsilon_X^*L).$$
Here derived internal Hom is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The canonical comparison is defined as follows: represent $K,L$ by complexes $\mathcal K^\bullet,\mathcal L^\bullet$, let $\mathcal L^\bullet\to\mathcal I^\bullet$ and $\epsilon_X^*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ be the fixed K-injective replacements of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], and use the Hom complexes of [def-pur-hom-complex]. In degree $n$, map $\epsilon_X^*\prod_p\mathcal Hom(\mathcal K^p,\mathcal I^{p+n})$ to $\prod_p\mathcal Hom(\epsilon_X^*\mathcal K^p,\epsilon_X^*\mathcal I^{p+n})$ by the projections and $h\mapsto\epsilon_X^*h$ on local sections, then postcompose with $\epsilon_X^*\mathcal I^\bullet\to\mathcal J^\bullet$. Since $\epsilon_X^*$ is exact, $\epsilon_X^*\mathcal L^\bullet\to\mathcal J^\bullet$ is a quasi-isomorphism, so the target complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\epsilon_X^*\mathcal K^\bullet,\mathcal J^\bullet)$ represents $R\mathcal Hom(\epsilon_X^*K,\epsilon_X^*L)$. Naturality is contravariant in $K$ and covariant in $L$, within the indicated domains. Neither quasi-coherence of $L$ nor a Noetherian hypothesis on $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08JP, lemma-descend-RHom, case (1); epsilon of equation-epsilon, exact by Tag 08H8, lemma-epsilon-flat; the canonical map of sites-cohomology.tex remark-prepare-fancy-base-change, written on Hom complexes.

proof.text: Put $T=\epsilon_X^*$. It is exact by [lem-sfb-derived-etale-zariski-equivalence], so applying it termwise preserves cohomology and quasi-isomorphisms: apply exactness to the kernels, images and quotients defining each cohomology sheaf. For arbitrary representatives $A,B$, put $I=I(B)$ and $J=I(TI)$. The projections and pullback of module maps give $c_{A,I}:T\mathcal Hom^\bullet(A,I)\to\mathcal Hom^\bullet(TA,TI)$. On a homogeneous family $f$, applying $T$ to $d_I f-(-1)^n f d_A$ gives $d_{TI}(Tf)-(-1)^n(Tf)d_{TA}$, so this is a chain map. Postcompose with $TI\to J$. The map $TB\to TI\to J$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $J$ is K-injective; hence the target is a representative of $R\mathcal Hom(TK,TL)$ by [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. All component maps commute with precomposition and postcomposition, and the replacements are functorial. Both resulting bifunctors invert quasi-isomorphisms by that definition and exactness of $T$. Thus the natural transformation descends through localization [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], contravariantly in $K$ and covariantly in $L$. This is precisely the comparison specified in the statement; no preservation of infinite products is used.

source.place: Tag 08JP, lemma-descend-RHom, proof of case (1); Hom-model normalization uses sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JI.

proof.text: It suffices to check that this map is a quasi-isomorphism over a Zariski open covering: the opens are also an etale covering, and a morphism of sheaves is an isomorphism when it is so on a covering. Derived internal Hom restricts to the Hom of the restricted objects by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-internal-hom-exact-restriction]. Pullback along $\epsilon$ commutes with restriction to opens by the comparison in [lem-trf-zariski-etale-functor-comparison-square], applied to an open immersion. The representatives in step 1 also restrict compatibly: K-injective complexes remain K-injective on slice sites by [lem-pur-kinjective-restrict-localized]. Projections, pullback of maps and postcomposition all restrict componentwise. Replacing a restricted resolution by the fixed local resolution gives the same derived morphism, by the representative independence in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. We may therefore use local representatives for both inputs and test the locally specified comparison.

source.place: Tag 08JP, lemma-descend-RHom, proof of case (1); Hom-model normalization uses sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JI.

proof.text: By the local finite-free formulation of pseudo-coherence in [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], choose such an open $U$ on which $K$ is represented by a complex $P$ of finite free $\mathcal O_U$-modules, with $P^p=0$ for $p>b$. Choose any representative $B$ of $L|_U$ and replace it by its good lower truncation $F$: put $F^q=0$ for $q<a$, $F^a=\operatorname{coker}(d_B^{a-1})$ and $F^q=B^q$ for $q>a$, with the induced differential. The quotient map $B\to F$ induces the identity on cohomology in degrees at least $a$ and an isomorphism between zero objects below $a$; hence it is a quasi-isomorphism by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Exactness of $T=\epsilon_U^*$ gives representatives $TP,TF$ of the pulled-back objects. Pullback sends $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$ to $\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}}^{\oplus r}$ and sends zero to zero, so $TP$ is again bounded above finite free and $TF$ is bounded below.

source.place: Tag 08JP, lemma-descend-RHom, proof of case (1); Hom-model normalization uses sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JI.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-model] first to the Zariski ringed site with $P,F$ and then to the small etale ringed site with $TP,TF$. Its hypotheses hold by step 3 (finite free is a direct summand of itself). Thus the two derived internal Homs are represented respectively by $H=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(P,F)$ and $H'=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(TP,TF)$. In degree $n$, only $a-n\leq p\leq b$ can contribute; the products in these Hom complexes are finite biproducts. Their differential is $d_F f-(-1)^n f d_P$.

source.place: Tag 08JP, lemma-descend-RHom, proof of case (1); Hom-model normalization uses sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JI.

proof.text: For a finite free $E=\mathcal O_U^{\oplus r}$ and any module sheaf $G$, evaluation on the $r$ basis sections identifies $\mathcal Hom(E,G)$ with $G^{\oplus r}$, directly from [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Since $T$ is exact and additive, it preserves finite biproducts. Under the identifications $TE=\mathcal O_{U,\mathrm{et}}^{\oplus r}$ and $T(G^{\oplus r})=(TG)^{\oplus r}$, the pullback-Hom map sends a tuple $(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$ to the same tuple. It is therefore an isomorphism, including $r=0$. Apply this to every $P^p,F^{p+n}$ and to the finite degree-$n$ biproduct of step 4. The resulting isomorphisms $TH^n\to(H')^n$ commute with the differential by the calculation in step 1, giving a chain isomorphism $c_{P,F}:TH\xrightarrow{\sim}H'$.

source.place: Tag 08JP, lemma-descend-RHom, proof of case (1); Hom-model normalization uses sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JI.

proof.text: Verify that the chain isomorphism just obtained represents the fixed comparison, rather than merely an unspecified isomorphism of its endpoints. Let $i:F\to I=I(F)$ and $j:TI\to J=I(TI)$ be the fixed augmentations. There is a commuting square whose upper arrow is $c_{P,F}:T\mathcal Hom(P,F)\to\mathcal Hom(TP,TF)$, whose left arrow is $T\mathcal Hom(P,i)$, whose right arrow is $\mathcal Hom(TP,j\circ Ti)$, and whose lower arrow is $\mathcal Hom(TP,j)\circ c_{P,I}$. Commutativity holds componentwise since pulling back a composite equals composing its pullbacks. The left arrow is a quasi-isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-bounded-free-rhom-quasi-iso] and exactness of $T$. The right arrow is a quasi-isomorphism by the same node on the etale site: $TP$ is bounded above finite free, $TF$ is bounded below, $J$ is K-injective and $j\circ Ti$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The node explicitly allows an unbounded K-injective target. After localization the vertical arrows are the canonical Hom-model identifications of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. The lower arrow is exactly step 1 on representatives $P,F$. It is an isomorphism because the upper arrow and both vertical arrows are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 08JP, lemma-descend-RHom, proof of case (1); Hom-model normalization uses sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08JI.

proof.text: Steps 2 and 6 show that the original comparison is locally a quasi-isomorphism on an open covering. Its maps on cohomology sheaves are therefore isomorphisms globally, so it is an isomorphism in the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Together with the naturality established in step 1 this proves the claimed natural isomorphism. The only restrictions used on the inputs were the local bounded-above finite-free model for $K$ and the lower cohomology bound for $L$; no quasi-coherence of $L$ or Noetherian assumption occurred.
